title: The Life of the Lord — from the Annunciation at Nazareth to the Ascension from Olivet
register: national mythology — the canon is true

segments.name: The Word Made Flesh — Annunciation and Nativity

stops.name: Nazareth — the house of Mary, the Annunciation
stops.campa: Into a poor house in an obscure Galilean town the archangel Gabriel is sent from God to a virgin betrothed to a carpenter named Joseph. He greets her: Hail, full of grace. She is troubled, and he tells her not to fear — she will conceive by the Holy Spirit and bear a son, Jesus, who will reign forever. She asks how, being a virgin. The power of the Most High will overshadow her. Then Mary bows: Be it done to me according to your word. Heaven waits on a girl's yes, and she gives it.
stops.quote: Behold the handmaid of the Lord; be it unto me according to thy word.
suggested_refs: Basilica of the Annunciation, Nazareth — the Grotto of the Annunciation
Fra Angelico, The Annunciation (San Marco)
Leonardo da Vinci, Annunciation (Uffizi)

stops.name: Ein Karem — the Visitation to Elizabeth
stops.campa: Mary rises and goes with haste into the hill country of Judah, to the house of Zacharias, where her kinswoman Elizabeth carries John in her old age. At Mary's greeting the babe leaps in Elizabeth's womb, and Elizabeth is filled with the Holy Spirit and cries out the blessedness of Mary among women. Then Mary answers with the song the Church has sung ever since — the Magnificat — her soul magnifying the Lord who scatters the proud and lifts the lowly. She stays three months, and returns to Nazareth.
stops.quote: My soul doth magnify the Lord, and my spirit hath rejoiced in God my Saviour.
suggested_refs: Church of the Visitation, Ein Karem
the Magnificat chanted at Vespers

stops.name: Bethlehem — the Grotto of the Nativity
stops.campa: Caesar Augustus decrees a census of all the world, and Joseph goes up from Nazareth to Bethlehem, the city of David, with Mary great with child. There is no room in the inn. In a cave among the beasts she brings forth her firstborn son, wraps him in swaddling clothes, and lays him in a manger. The maker of the stars is laid in a feed-trough for oxen. Heaven does not announce it to kings; the Lord of all enters the world unnoticed, in the cold, and the night holds its breath over a stable.
stops.quote: And she brought forth her firstborn son, and wrapped him in swaddling clothes, and laid him in a manger; because there was no room for them in the inn.
suggested_refs: Church of the Nativity, Bethlehem — the silver Star of Bethlehem marking the birthplace
Byzantine mosaics of the Nativity

stops.name: Shepherds' Field, Beit Sahour — the angels to the shepherds
stops.campa: In the fields east of Bethlehem shepherds keep watch over their flocks by night. The angel of the Lord comes upon them, and the glory of the Lord shines round about, and they are sore afraid. Fear not, the angel says, I bring good tidings of great joy: unto you is born this day a Saviour, Christ the Lord. And suddenly a multitude of the heavenly host praises God. When the angels go, the shepherds run to Bethlehem and find the babe in the manger, and they are the first to worship him — the poor, called first.
stops.quote: Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace, good will toward men.
suggested_refs: Shepherds' Field, Beit Sahour — Franciscan Chapel of the Angels
medieval Nativity plays

stops.name: Bethlehem — the Adoration of the Magi
stops.campa: Wise men come from the east to Jerusalem, asking where is he that is born King of the Jews, for they have seen his star and come to worship him. Herod is troubled, and the scribes point them to Bethlehem. The star goes before them and stands over the place where the young child is. They fall down and worship, and open their treasures: gold for a king, frankincense for God, myrrh for one who will die. Warned in a dream not to return to Herod, they depart into their own country another way.
stops.quote: Where is he that is born King of the Jews? for we have seen his star in the east, and are come to worship him.
suggested_refs: Shrine of the Three Kings, Cologne Cathedral
Gentile da Fabriano, Adoration of the Magi
the Epiphany feast

stops.name: Jerusalem — the Presentation in the Temple, Simeon and Anna
stops.campa: On the fortieth day they bring the child up to Jerusalem to present him to the Lord and offer the sacrifice of the poor, a pair of turtledoves. The just and devout Simeon, promised he would not die before he saw the Christ, is led by the Spirit into the Temple, takes the child in his arms, and blesses God with the song the Church sings at nightfall — now lettest thou thy servant depart in peace. He warns Mary that a sword shall pierce her own soul. And Anna the aged prophetess, who departs not from the Temple, gives thanks and speaks of him to all who look for redemption.
stops.quote: Lord, now lettest thou thy servant depart in peace, according to thy word: for mine eyes have seen thy salvation.
suggested_refs: the Temple Mount, Jerusalem
the Nunc Dimittis sung at Compline
Rembrandt, Simeon in the Temple

segments.name: The Flight and the Hidden Years

stops.name: Bethlehem — the Massacre of the Innocents
stops.campa: Herod, mocked of the wise men, is exceeding wroth, and sends soldiers to slay all the children in Bethlehem and its coasts from two years old and under. A cry goes up in Ramah — Rachel weeping for her children, and would not be comforted, because they are not. The first blood shed for Christ is the blood of infants who cannot yet speak his name; the Church counts them the first martyrs, the Holy Innocents, who die in his place while he is carried away to safety.
stops.quote: In Rama was there a voice heard, lamentation, and weeping, and great mourning, Rachel weeping for her children, and would not be comforted, because they are not.
suggested_refs: Grotto of the Holy Innocents beneath the Church of the Nativity
Giotto, Massacre of the Innocents (Scrovegni Chapel)

stops.name: Cairo — Abu Serga, the Holy Family in Egypt
stops.campa: An angel of the Lord appears to Joseph in a dream: Arise, take the young child and his mother, and flee into Egypt, for Herod will seek the child to destroy him. By night they go down into Egypt, out of the promised land into the house of ancient bondage, that the word might be fulfilled: Out of Egypt have I called my son. Coptic tradition follows their long road from the Delta up the Nile, resting in caves and by wells; at Old Cairo they shelter in the crypt where Abu Serga now stands.
stops.quote: When he arose, he took the young child and his mother by night, and departed into Egypt.
suggested_refs: Church of St Sergius and Bacchus (Abu Serga), Coptic Cairo — the crypt of the Holy Family
the Coptic Holy Family pilgrimage route

stops.name: Deir al-Muharraq, Qusqam — the southernmost refuge
stops.campa: Coptic tradition brings the Holy Family up the Nile to the mountain of Qusqam in Upper Egypt, the farthest point of their exile, where they dwell some six months in a small dwelling now enclosed in the ancient church of the Monastery of the Muharraq. Here, the Copts hold, the altar-stone is the very rock on which the child slept, and an angel later comes again to Joseph in a dream with word that those who sought the child's life are dead. The place is called a second Bethlehem.
suggested_refs: Monastery of the Holy Virgin (Deir al-Muharraq), Asyut — the Church of the Blessed Virgin over the Family's dwelling
sources: Coptic Orthodox tradition of the Holy Family

stops.name: Nazareth — the return and the hidden childhood
stops.campa: When Herod is dead, the angel bids Joseph return; but hearing that Archelaus reigns in Judea, he turns aside into Galilee and settles again in Nazareth, that the child might be called a Nazarene. There, in a village of no account, the Lord of glory grows up as a carpenter's son. He learns the plane and the adze at Joseph's bench, keeps the Sabbath in the little synagogue, and is subject to his parents. The Gospels draw a curtain over these years: the Word is silent, waxing strong, filled with wisdom.
stops.quote: And the child grew, and waxed strong in spirit, filled with wisdom: and the grace of God was upon him.
suggested_refs: Church of St Joseph, Nazareth — traditional site of the carpenter's workshop
Nazareth Village

stops.name: Jerusalem — the boy Jesus in the Temple, at twelve
stops.campa: At twelve years old Jesus goes up with his parents to Jerusalem for the Passover. When they return, the boy tarries behind, and after a day's journey they miss him and turn back in sorrow. After three days they find him in the Temple, sitting among the doctors, hearing them and asking questions, and all are astonished at his understanding. His mother reproaches him gently; the child answers with his first recorded words, and they do not yet understand. Then he goes down with them and is subject to them, and Mary keeps all these sayings in her heart.
stops.quote: How is it that ye sought me? wist ye not that I must be about my Father's business?
suggested_refs: the Temple Mount, Jerusalem
Duccio, Christ among the Doctors (Maestà)

segments.name: The Beginning of the Gospel — Baptism and Wilderness

stops.name: Qasr el-Yahud, the Jordan — the Baptism of the Lord
stops.campa: John baptizes in the Jordan, crying repentance and pointing beyond himself: there comes one mightier than I, whose shoes I am not worthy to unloose. Jesus comes from Galilee to be baptized, and John forbids him — I have need to be baptized of thee. But Jesus answers, Suffer it to be so now. And when he comes up out of the water, the heavens are opened, and the Spirit of God descends like a dove and lights upon him, and a voice from heaven speaks. The whole Trinity is manifest at once over the river: Father, Son, and Spirit.
stops.quote: This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased.
suggested_refs: Qasr el-Yahud baptismal site on the Jordan
Bethany Beyond the Jordan (Al-Maghtas), UNESCO site
Piero della Francesca, Baptism of Christ

stops.name: Mount of Temptation, Jericho — the forty days
stops.campa: The Spirit drives him up into the wilderness, into the barren hills above Jericho, where he fasts forty days and forty nights and is afterward hungry. The tempter comes: turn these stones to bread; cast thyself from the pinnacle of the Temple; fall down and worship me, and all the kingdoms of the world are thine. To each Jesus answers with the word of God, and refuses. Then the devil leaves him, and behold, angels come and minister unto him. The new Adam stands where the first Adam fell, and does not fall.
stops.quote: Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceedeth out of the mouth of God.
suggested_refs: Monastery of the Temptation (Deir al-Quruntul) on Jebel Quruntul above Jericho
Duccio, The Temptation on the Mount

segments.name: The Galilean Ministry — Signs and the Kingdom

stops.name: Cana of Galilee — water into wine, the first sign
stops.campa: There is a marriage in Cana, and Jesus and his mother and disciples are called. The wine fails, and Mary tells him. His hour is not yet come, he says, yet at her word the servants fill six stone jars with water to the brim. Draw out now, he tells them, and bear to the governor of the feast. The water has become wine — the best wine, kept until last. This is the beginning of miracles; he manifests his glory, and his disciples believe on him. The first sign is joy poured out at a wedding, abundance where there was lack.
stops.quote: Whatsoever he saith unto you, do it.
suggested_refs: Wedding Church at Cana (Kafr Kanna)
the stone water-jars of Cana
Giotto, Marriage at Cana (Scrovegni)

stops.name: Sychar — the Samaritan woman at Jacob's Well
stops.campa: Wearied with the journey, he sits alone at Jacob's Well in Samaria at the sixth hour, and asks a woman come to draw, Give me to drink. She marvels that a Jew speaks to a Samaritan woman. He offers her living water, that whoever drinks of it shall never thirst but have a well springing up to everlasting life. He tells her all she ever did — five husbands, and he that she has now not her own — and she perceives he is a prophet. He reveals that God is Spirit and must be worshipped in spirit and truth, and to her, an outsider, he says plainly: I am he.
stops.quote: Whosoever drinketh of the water that I shall give him shall never thirst; but the water that I shall give him shall be in him a well of water springing up into everlasting life.
suggested_refs: Jacob's Well at Bir Ya'qub, in the crypt of the Church of St Photini (Nablus)
Byzantine icon of St Photini the Samaritan

stops.name: Capernaum — the town of his own, and the calling of the Twelve
stops.campa: Leaving Nazareth, Jesus comes and dwells in Capernaum by the sea, and makes it his own city. Walking by the Sea of Galilee he sees Simon and Andrew casting a net, and James and John mending theirs, and calls them: Follow me. Straightway they leave nets and father and follow him. In the synagogue he teaches as one having authority, casts out an unclean spirit, and heals Peter's wife's mother of a fever; and at evening the whole town is gathered at the door, and he heals all their sick. From the twelve he calls, he makes apostles.
stops.quote: Follow me, and I will make you fishers of men.
suggested_refs: the White Synagogue of Capernaum
the House of Peter (octagonal church), Capernaum

stops.name: Mount of Beatitudes — the Sermon on the Mount
stops.campa: Seeing the multitudes, he goes up into a mountain, and his disciples come, and he opens his mouth and teaches them. Blessed are the poor in spirit; blessed are they that mourn; blessed are the meek, the merciful, the pure in heart, the peacemakers, the persecuted. He gives them the Lord's Prayer, tells them to love their enemies, to lay up treasure in heaven, to seek first the kingdom of God. The crowds are astonished, for he teaches with authority. On a green hillside above the lake, the new law is given, higher than Sinai's.
stops.quote: Blessed are the poor in spirit: for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.
suggested_refs: Church of the Beatitudes on the Mount of Beatitudes
the octagonal chapel above the Sea of Galilee

stops.name: Galilee — the cleansing of the leper
stops.campa: A leper comes to him, an outcast forbidden to draw near any man, and kneels down: Lord, if thou wilt, thou canst make me clean. Moved with compassion, Jesus does what the law forbids — he puts forth his hand and touches him. I will; be thou clean. Immediately the leprosy departs, and the man is whole. The touch that should have defiled the healer instead heals the leper; uncleanness flows backward. Jesus charges him to show himself to the priest, but the man cannot keep silent, and the fame of it spreads through all the region.
stops.quote: I will; be thou clean.
suggested_refs: Sea of Galilee shore, Galilee
Byzantine healing-miracle mosaics

stops.name: Nain — the raising of the widow's son
stops.campa: As he comes near the gate of the town of Nain, a dead man is carried out, the only son of his mother, and she a widow, and a great crowd of the town with her. When the Lord sees her, he has compassion on her and says, Weep not. He comes and touches the bier, and the bearers stand still, and he speaks to the corpse: Young man, I say unto thee, Arise. And he that was dead sits up and begins to speak, and Jesus delivers him to his mother. Fear seizes them all, and they glorify God, saying a great prophet is risen among us, and God has visited his people.
stops.quote: Young man, I say unto thee, Arise.
suggested_refs: the village of Nein (Nain) on the slope of the Hill of Moreh
Franciscan church at Nain

stops.name: Capernaum — the paralytic let down through the roof
stops.campa: The house is so thronged that no one can come near the door. Four men carry a paralytic on a bed, and finding no way in, they climb the roof, break it open, and let him down before Jesus. Seeing their faith he says, Son, thy sins be forgiven thee. The scribes murmur — who can forgive sins but God alone? To show he has that power, he turns to the man: Arise, take up thy bed, and walk. And immediately he rises, takes up his bed, and goes forth before them all, and they are amazed and glorify God.
stops.quote: Arise, take up thy bed, and go thy way into thine house.
suggested_refs: the House of Peter at Capernaum
the ruins of first-century Capernaum

stops.name: The Sea of Galilee — the stilling of the storm
stops.campa: They put out across the lake at evening, and Jesus falls asleep in the stern on a pillow. A great tempest rises; the waves beat into the boat, and it fills, and the disciples are afraid. They wake him: Master, carest thou not that we perish? He arises, rebukes the wind, and says to the sea, Peace, be still. And the wind ceases, and there is a great calm. Then he asks them why they are so fearful, how it is they have no faith. And they fear exceedingly, saying one to another, What manner of man is this, that even wind and sea obey him?
stops.quote: Peace, be still.
suggested_refs: the Sea of Galilee (Lake Kinneret)
the Galilee Boat (first-century fishing boat) at Kibbutz Ginosar
Rembrandt, Storm on the Sea of Galilee

stops.name: Kursi (Gergesa) — the Gerasene demoniac
stops.campa: On the far shore, among the tombs, a man possessed of a legion of demons meets him — one whom no chains could bind, crying out and cutting himself with stones night and day. The demons fall down before Jesus and beg not to be sent into the abyss but into a herd of swine. He gives them leave; the unclean spirits enter the swine, and the whole herd, two thousand, run violently down the steep place into the sea and drown. The man is found sitting, clothed, in his right mind. He begs to follow; Jesus sends him home to tell what great things God has done.
stops.quote: Go home to thy friends, and tell them how great things the Lord hath done for thee.
suggested_refs: Kursi archaeological site and Byzantine monastery on the eastern shore
the steep bank at Gergesa

stops.name: Capernaum — the raising of Jairus's daughter
stops.campa: Jairus, a ruler of the synagogue, falls at his feet: my little daughter lies at the point of death, come and lay thy hands on her. On the way a woman with a twelve-year issue of blood touches the hem of his garment and is healed, for virtue goes out of him. Then word comes that the girl is dead. Fear not, only believe, he tells the father. He puts out the mourners, takes her by the hand, and speaks. Talitha cumi — Damsel, arise. Straightway the girl of twelve rises and walks, and he bids them give her food. Her parents are astonished.
stops.quote: Talitha cumi; which is, being interpreted, Damsel, I say unto thee, arise.
suggested_refs: Capernaum synagogue and lakeshore
the Woman with the Issue of Blood (Banias statue tradition)

stops.name: Tabgha — the feeding of the five thousand
stops.campa: The multitude has followed him into a desert place, and evening comes with nothing to eat. Send them away, the disciples say. But he answers, Give ye them to eat. They have only five loaves and two fishes. He bids the people sit down on the green grass in ranks, takes the loaves, looks up to heaven, blesses and breaks them, and gives to the disciples to set before the crowd. All eat and are filled — about five thousand men, beside women and children — and they take up twelve baskets of fragments. From a boy's lunch, a feast for a nation.
stops.quote: They need not depart; give ye them to eat.
suggested_refs: Church of the Multiplication, Tabgha — the mosaic of the loaves and fishes
the Byzantine mosaic floor at Tabgha

stops.name: The Sea of Galilee — walking on the water
stops.campa: He sends the disciples ahead by boat and goes up alone into a mountain to pray. In the fourth watch of the night, the boat tossed with waves and the wind contrary, he comes to them walking upon the sea. They are terrified, crying out for a ghost; but he says, Be of good cheer, it is I; be not afraid. Peter answers, Lord, bid me come — and he steps out onto the water and walks toward Jesus, until, seeing the wind, he is afraid and begins to sink and cries, Lord, save me. Jesus stretches out his hand and catches him, and the wind ceases.
stops.quote: Be of good cheer; it is I; be not afraid.
suggested_refs: the Sea of Galilee (Lake Kinneret)
Ivan Aivazovsky, Jesus Walking on Water

segments.name: The Turning Toward Jerusalem — Confession and Glory

stops.name: Caesarea Philippi (Banias) — Peter's confession
stops.campa: At the foot of Hermon, by the springs of the Jordan and the great rock-shrine of Pan, Jesus asks his disciples, Whom do men say that I am? Some say John, some Elias, some Jeremias. But whom say ye that I am? Simon Peter answers, Thou art the Christ, the Son of the living God. Blessed art thou, Simon, for flesh and blood has not revealed this, but my Father. Thou art Peter, and upon this rock I will build my church. From here Jesus begins to tell them plainly that he must go up to Jerusalem, suffer, be killed, and rise the third day.
stops.quote: Thou art Peter, and upon this rock I will build my church; and the gates of hell shall not prevail against it.
suggested_refs: Banias (Caesarea Philippi) — the cave and niches of the Sanctuary of Pan
the springs of the Jordan at Banias

stops.name: Mount Tabor — the Transfiguration
stops.campa: After six days he takes Peter, James, and John up into a high mountain apart, and is transfigured before them: his face shines as the sun, and his raiment becomes white as the light. Moses and Elias appear, talking with him of his coming departure at Jerusalem. Peter, half-asleep and bewildered, offers to build three tabernacles. Then a bright cloud overshadows them, and out of the cloud a voice speaks the same word heard at the Jordan. The disciples fall on their faces, sore afraid; Jesus touches them: Arise, be not afraid. And they see no man save Jesus only.
stops.quote: This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased; hear ye him.
suggested_refs: Church of the Transfiguration on Mount Tabor
Raphael, The Transfiguration (Vatican)
the icon of the Transfiguration with the mandorla of light

stops.name: Bethany — the raising of Lazarus
stops.campa: Lazarus, whom he loves, has died and lain four days in the tomb. Martha meets him: Lord, if thou hadst been here, my brother had not died. Jesus weeps. Then he comes to the grave, a cave with a stone against it, and bids them take the stone away, though Martha warns of the stench. Lifting his eyes he gives thanks, then cries with a loud voice, Lazarus, come forth. And the dead man comes out, bound hand and foot with graveclothes. Loose him, and let him go. Many believe; and this last and greatest sign hardens the council against him.
stops.quote: I am the resurrection, and the life: he that believeth in me, though he were dead, yet shall he live.
suggested_refs: the Tomb of Lazarus at Bethany (Al-Eizariya)
Church of Saint Lazarus, Bethany
Giotto, Raising of Lazarus (Scrovegni)

stops.name: Jerusalem — the woman taken in adultery
stops.campa: In the Temple at dawn the scribes and Pharisees bring a woman taken in adultery and set her in the midst, to tempt him — Moses commanded to stone such; what sayest thou? Jesus stoops and writes with his finger on the ground, as though he heard them not. When they press him, he lifts himself and speaks one sentence, then stoops again. Convicted by their own conscience, they go out one by one, the eldest first, until she is left alone with him. Neither do I condemn thee, he tells her; go, and sin no more. Mercy without excuse, and judgment turned back on the judges.
stops.quote: He that is without sin among you, let him first cast a stone at her.
suggested_refs: the Temple Mount and the Court of the Women, Jerusalem
Bruegel, Christ and the Woman Taken in Adultery

stops.name: Jericho — Zacchaeus and blind Bartimaeus
stops.campa: Passing through Jericho on the way up to Jerusalem, blind Bartimaeus sits begging by the road and cries out, Jesus, thou son of David, have mercy on me; and Jesus restores his sight, for his faith has made him whole. And Zacchaeus, chief among the publicans and small of stature, climbs a sycamore tree to see him. Jesus looks up: Zacchaeus, make haste and come down, for today I must abide at thy house. The crowd murmurs that he goes to a sinner, but Zacchaeus repents and gives half his goods to the poor, and salvation comes to that house.
stops.quote: For the Son of man is come to seek and to save that which was lost.
suggested_refs: the sycamore of Zacchaeus, Jericho
Tell es-Sultan and Roman Jericho

segments.name: The Passion — Jerusalem and the Cross

stops.name: Bethany — the anointing at Simon's house
stops.campa: Six days before the Passover, at supper in Bethany, Mary takes a pound of very costly ointment of pure nard and anoints his feet and wipes them with her hair, and the house is filled with the fragrance. Judas objects — it might have been sold and given to the poor — for he keeps the bag and is a thief. But Jesus defends her: Let her alone; against the day of my burying she has kept this. The poor ye have always, but me ye have not always. She has anointed his body beforehand for the grave; wheresoever the Gospel is preached, this shall be told for a memorial of her.
stops.quote: She hath done what she could: she is come aforehand to anoint my body to the burying.
suggested_refs: Bethany (Al-Eizariya) — house of Simon the Leper
the alabaster jar of nard

stops.name: Bethphage — the entry into Jerusalem on Palm Sunday
stops.campa: At Bethphage on the Mount of Olives he sends for a colt whereon never man sat, and rides down toward the city as the prophet foretold — the king coming meek and lowly. A great multitude spreads garments and palm branches in the way, and the whole crowd cries Hosanna to the son of David. When he draws near and sees the city, he weeps over it, for it knows not the day of its visitation. The Pharisees bid him rebuke his disciples; he answers that if these hold their peace, the very stones would cry out.
stops.quote: Blessed is he that cometh in the name of the Lord: Hosanna in the highest.
suggested_refs: Church of Bethphage on the Mount of Olives
Dominus Flevit church (where he wept over Jerusalem)
the Palm Sunday procession down the Mount of Olives

stops.name: Jerusalem — the cleansing of the Temple
stops.campa: He goes into the Temple and finds it a marketplace — the money-changers at their tables, sellers of oxen and sheep and doves. He makes a scourge of small cords, overthrows the tables, pours out the changers' money, and drives them all out, saying his Father's house has been made a den of thieves. The blind and the lame come to him in the Temple, and he heals them. The chief priests, seeing the wonders and the children crying Hosanna, are indignant and seek how they might destroy him, but fear the people, for all hang on his words.
stops.quote: It is written, My house shall be called the house of prayer; but ye have made it a den of thieves.
suggested_refs: the Temple Mount, Jerusalem
the Court of the Gentiles
El Greco, Christ Driving the Money Changers

stops.name: The Cenacle, Mount Zion — the Last Supper
stops.campa: In a large upper room, furnished and prepared, he keeps the Passover with the Twelve. He rises from supper, girds himself with a towel, and washes their feet — the Lord and Master kneeling before his servants. Then, as they eat, he takes bread, blesses and breaks it: Take, eat, this is my body. And the cup: This is my blood of the new testament, shed for many. Do this in remembrance of me. He foretells that one of them will betray him and that Peter will deny him thrice before cockcrow, and gives them a new commandment: that they love one another.
stops.quote: This is my body which is given for you: this do in remembrance of me.
suggested_refs: the Cenacle (Upper Room) on Mount Zion
Leonardo da Vinci, The Last Supper
the institution of the Eucharist

stops.name: Gethsemane — the Agony in the Garden
stops.campa: He comes with them to a garden at the foot of Olivet called Gethsemane, and begins to be sorrowful and very heavy — my soul is exceeding sorrowful, even unto death. He goes a stone's cast apart, falls on his face, and prays that the cup might pass; yet not my will but thine be done. His sweat becomes as it were great drops of blood falling to the ground, and an angel from heaven strengthens him. Thrice he finds the disciples sleeping. Then Judas comes with a band and lanterns and kisses him — and by that sign they take him and bind him.
stops.quote: O my Father, if this cup may not pass away from me, except I drink it, thy will be done.
suggested_refs: the Garden of Gethsemane and its ancient olive trees
Church of All Nations (Basilica of the Agony) over the Rock of the Agony
Bellini, The Agony in the Garden

stops.name: Jerusalem — before Caiaphas, and Peter's denial
stops.campa: They lead him to the house of Caiaphas the high priest, where the council seeks false witness to put him to death. When the high priest adjures him — art thou the Christ, the Son of the Blessed? — Jesus answers, I am, and ye shall see the Son of man coming in the clouds. Caiaphas rends his clothes, crying blasphemy, and they spit on him and buffet him. Below in the courtyard, warming himself at the fire, Peter thrice denies that he knows him; and the cock crows, and Peter, meeting the Lord's look, goes out and weeps bitterly.
stops.quote: I am: and ye shall see the Son of man sitting on the right hand of power, and coming in the clouds of heaven.
suggested_refs: Church of St Peter in Gallicantu (house of Caiaphas)
the pit and the Sacred Steps below Gallicantu

stops.name: Jerusalem — Pilate, Herod, and Ecce Homo
stops.campa: At dawn they deliver him to Pilate the governor. Pilate finds no fault, and hearing he is a Galilean sends him to Herod, who mocks him with a gorgeous robe and sends him back. Pilate scourges him; the soldiers plait a crown of thorns and press it on his head, and hail him King of the Jews. Then Pilate brings him out, wearing the thorns and the purple, and shows him to the crowd — Behold the man. But they cry, Crucify him. Pilate washes his hands, saying he is innocent of this blood, and delivers Jesus to be crucified.
stops.quote: Behold the man!
suggested_refs: the Ecce Homo Arch on the Via Dolorosa
the Lithostrotos (Pavement) beneath the Convent of the Sisters of Zion
Antonio Ciseri, Ecce Homo

stops.name: The Via Dolorosa — the way of the cross
stops.campa: Bearing his cross, he goes out through the city toward the place of a skull. Under its weight he falls, and the soldiers compel Simon of Cyrene, coming out of the country, to carry it after him. A great company of women follow, bewailing him; he turns and says, Daughters of Jerusalem, weep not for me, but weep for yourselves and for your children. Tradition marks the stations along the sorrowful way — his meeting with his mother, the veil of Veronica, his falls — the last long walk of the condemned through the narrow streets to Golgotha.
stops.quote: Daughters of Jerusalem, weep not for me, but weep for yourselves, and for your children.
suggested_refs: the Via Dolorosa and its Stations of the Cross, Old City of Jerusalem
the tradition of the Fourteen Stations

stops.name: Golgotha — the Crucifixion
stops.campa: At the place called Golgotha they crucify him at the third hour, between two thieves, and over his head the title: Jesus of Nazareth, King of the Jews. He prays for his killers — Father, forgive them, they know not what they do. He gives his mother to the beloved disciple. From the sixth hour darkness covers the land until the ninth, and he cries out the psalm of dereliction, and thirsts, and at last, It is finished, and gives up the ghost. The veil of the Temple is rent in twain from top to bottom, the earth quakes, and the centurion says, Truly this was the Son of God.
stops.quote: Father, into thy hands I commend my spirit.
suggested_refs: the Rock of Calvary (Golgotha) in the Church of the Holy Sepulchre
Grünewald, Isenheim Crucifixion
the Stone of Anointing

stops.name: The Tomb of Joseph of Arimathea — the burial
stops.campa: As evening comes, Joseph of Arimathea, an honourable counsellor and a secret disciple, goes boldly to Pilate and begs the body. With Nicodemus, who brings myrrh and aloes about a hundred pound weight, he takes the body down, wraps it in fine linen with the spices, and lays it in his own new tomb hewn out of the rock, wherein never man was laid, in a garden near the place of crucifixion. They roll a great stone against the door. The women from Galilee behold where he is laid, and the Sabbath begins over a sealed and guarded grave.
stops.quote: There laid they Jesus therefore because of the Jews' preparation day; for the sepulchre was nigh at hand.
suggested_refs: the Edicule of the Holy Sepulchre over the Tomb of Christ
the Stone of Anointing, Church of the Holy Sepulchre

stops.name: The Garden Tomb — the empty tomb, Easter morning
stops.campa: Very early on the first day of the week, while it is yet dark, Mary Magdalene and the other women come with spices and find the great stone rolled away and the tomb empty. An angel with a countenance like lightning sits upon the stone and speaks: Fear not; ye seek Jesus who was crucified. He is not here, for he is risen, as he said. Come, see the place where the Lord lay. And go quickly, tell his disciples. They flee from the sepulchre with fear and great joy, running to bring the news that death is undone.
stops.quote: He is not here: for he is risen, as he said. Come, see the place where the Lord lay.
suggested_refs: the Empty Tomb (Edicule) in the Church of the Holy Sepulchre
the Anastasis icon (Harrowing of Hell)
Piero della Francesca, Resurrection

stops.name: The Garden — the risen Lord to Mary Magdalene
stops.campa: Mary lingers weeping at the tomb, and stooping in, sees two angels where the body had lain. Turning, she sees Jesus standing, but knows him not, supposing him the gardener. Sir, if thou hast borne him hence, tell me where. Then he speaks her name — Mary. She turns and cries, Rabboni, Master, and would clasp him. Touch me not, he says, for I am not yet ascended; but go to my brethren and say I ascend unto my Father and your Father. And Mary Magdalene runs to the disciples, the first witness of the Resurrection, apostle to the apostles.
stops.quote: Touch me not; for I am not yet ascended to my Father: but go to my brethren.
suggested_refs: the Noli me tangere garden tradition
Fra Angelico, Noli Me Tangere (San Marco)
Titian, Noli me Tangere

stops.name: The road to Emmaus — the breaking of bread
stops.campa: That same day two disciples walk to a village called Emmaus, reasoning sadly of all that has happened. Jesus himself draws near and goes with them, but their eyes are held that they do not know him. He opens the scriptures, beginning at Moses, showing how the Christ must suffer and enter into glory; their hearts burn within them. At evening he sits at meat, takes bread, blesses, breaks, and gives it — and in that gesture their eyes are opened, and they know him, and he vanishes. They rise that same hour and return to Jerusalem to tell it.
stops.quote: Did not our heart burn within us, while he talked with us by the way, and while he opened to us the scriptures?
suggested_refs: Emmaus at El-Qubeibeh (Franciscan Emmaus)
Emmaus-Nicopolis
Caravaggio, Supper at Emmaus

stops.name: Jerusalem — the upper room, and doubting Thomas
stops.campa: The doors being shut for fear, Jesus comes and stands in the midst: Peace be unto you. He shows them his hands and his side, and they are glad. But Thomas was not there, and will not believe unless he sees and touches the wounds. Eight days later Jesus comes again through the closed doors and turns to him: Reach hither thy finger, and behold my hands; and be not faithless, but believing. Thomas answers with the great confession, My Lord and my God. And Jesus blesses those who have not seen and yet have believed.
stops.quote: Thomas, because thou hast seen me, thou hast believed: blessed are they that have not seen, and yet have believed.
suggested_refs: the Cenacle, Mount Zion
Caravaggio, The Incredulity of Saint Thomas

stops.name: The Sea of Galilee — the third appearing, and Peter restored
stops.campa: By the Sea of Tiberias the disciples fish all night and take nothing. At dawn a figure on the shore bids them cast on the right side, and the net fills with a hundred and fifty-three great fishes. It is the Lord, and Peter plunges into the sea to reach him. On the shore a fire of coals is laid, with fish and bread, and Jesus says, Come and dine. Then thrice he asks, Simon, lovest thou me? and thrice Peter answers yes, and thrice is charged: Feed my sheep. The threefold denial is healed by a threefold love.
stops.quote: Simon, son of Jonas, lovest thou me? ... Feed my sheep.
suggested_refs: the Church of the Primacy of Peter, Tabgha — the Mensa Christi rock
the shore of the Sea of Galilee at Tabgha

stops.name: The Mount of Olives — the Ascension
stops.campa: He leads them out as far as Bethany, to the Mount of Olives, and lifts up his hands and blesses them. All power in heaven and earth is given to him; go ye therefore and teach all nations, baptizing them, and lo, I am with you always, even unto the end of the world. And while he blesses them he is parted from them and taken up, and a cloud receives him out of their sight. As they gaze steadfastly into heaven, two men in white apparel stand by: this same Jesus shall so come again as ye have seen him go. They return to Jerusalem with great joy.
stops.quote: And, lo, I am with you alway, even unto the end of the world.
suggested_refs: the Chapel of the Ascension (Imprint of the Foot) on the Mount of Olives
the Ascension icon
Giotto, Ascension (Scrovegni)
